codes.notes: Hippalus combines iterative categorical, numeric and hierarchical facet constraints with explicit best/worst/preferTo preferences. New controls set desired result count R, maximum ranking-bucket size MB, inner-bucket ordering and preference for common or rare values. An object-level explain button reveals score components and satisfied preferences.

SmartFSRank preserves preference buckets, fills a short focus with approximately matching objects scored against hard constraints (including taxonomy-based Jaccard similarity), and breaks large ranking ties using contextual/global discrimination statistics. The interface distinguishes ranked buckets and shows per-object/per-facet score explanations; approximate results can violate hard constraints.

codes.notes: For the 382-object hotel dataset the reported average hard-constraint action latency rises from 2 ms without automatic ranking to approximately 20 ms with it. Ranking complexity is O(N*K) for objects N and facets K. Indexing and algorithms for very large datasets remain future work.

For the 382-object hotel dataset the reported average hard-constraint action latency rises from 2 ms without automatic ranking to approximately 20 ms with it. Ranking complexity is O(N*K) for objects N and facets K. Indexing and algorithms for very large datasets remain future work.

Two computational simulations use the same 382 hotels and 18 facets, treating each hotel as a target and applying hard constraints or best-type soft constraints until it reaches top K. Common-value ranking improves reported constraint counts; rare-value ranking worsens them. These simulated users are not recruited participants. A separate runtime claim and ranking complexity are reported.

limitations: No recruited or measured human workflow outcomes; simulations use authored target-object constraints.
